attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1/node2/node3 (node1 initially primary, node2/node3 standbys via pg_basebackup + replication slots). Exercised a full failover: stopped node1's postgres to simulate primary loss, promoted node2 (verified zero committed-data loss), repointed node3 to follow node2, and rebuilt node1 as a fresh standby of node2 (pg_rewind was unavailable due to missing checksums/wal_log_hints, so used pg_basebackup instead). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node3, then node2 (primary) one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirming changed boot_id and full replication/data recovery after each before proceeding to the next. Final state: node2 = writable primary, node1 & node3 = streaming standbys, all caught up to the latest LSN and identical row counts/data.
